shared_binary_sufficiency.question: can one mode binary be shared between the TSO and DSO copies of the same physical ESS?
shared_binary_sufficiency.what_the_couplings_force: the interface_ess_p / interface_ess_q rows force shared_es_pnet_TSO == shared_es_pnet_DSO (both networks are on a 100 MVA base, so the conversion is the identity).  They force the NET power to agree; they do not force the (pch, pdch) split to agree.
shared_binary_sufficiency.physical_answer: physically the two copies are one device, so a common mode is the correct physics and one binary per physical ESS / year / day / period is what the device actually has.
shared_binary_sufficiency.mathematical_answer: NOT unconditionally valid as an OUTER approximation of the two-copy H1 set.  Write pi for the common net power.  A charge-dominant copy has pdch <= delta*S, hence pch = pi + pdch in [pi, pi + delta*S].  A discharge-dominant copy has pch <= delta*S, hence pdch = pch - pi >= 0 requires pi <= delta*S.  The two copies can therefore legitimately sit in OPPOSITE modes precisely when |pi| <= delta*S.  Outside that band the modes must agree and one shared binary loses nothing; inside it, a shared binary would exclude combinations that are H1-feasible for each copy separately, which breaks the lower-bound guarantee in that band.
rigorous_options: 1728 binaries (one per network copy) -- unconditionally a valid outer approximation;
864 binaries (one per physical ESS) -- valid only with an explicit argument that the |pnet| <= delta*S band contributes nothing, which has NOT been proved here;
shared_binary_sufficiency.recommendation: if the MISOCP were ever built, start from 864 shared binaries for tractability and treat the |pnet| <= 0.01*S band as a documented approximation, or use 1728 for a formally clean bound.  Do not assume the shared form is free.

execution_status.why: D4 is the gate for D5, and D4 fired against it: fixing every ESS mode moved the full-model objective by 0.049 % and closed 0.42 % of the gap to the polished nonlinear feasible point.  Because Q_MISOCP <= Q_fixed_mode, the unrestricted MISOCP optimum cannot close more.  Running MI-1..MI-4 would only measure the cost of confirming a conclusion already reached.
